\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পৌঁছানো} (poũchhāno)}{পৌঁছানো (poũchhāno)}]{\bn{পৌঁছানো} (poũchhāno) — to arrive; to reach}

\label{lesson:BN-C280-pouchhano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to burn down, then the Bengali for an explosion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পৌঁছানো}}
\textbf{\bn{পৌঁছানো}} — \emph{poũchhāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrive; to reach\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমরা} \bn{কত} \bn{তাড়াতাড়ি} \bn{পৌঁছাব}, \bn{সেটা} \bn{তোমার} \bn{ওপর} \bn{নির্ভর} \bn{করে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmrā kôtô tāṛātāṛi poũchhābô, seṭā tomār opôr nirbhôr kôre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
How fast we get there is up to you.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{দমকল} \bn{পৌঁছাল}, \emph{sei dômkôl poũchhālô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পৌঁছানো}} (\emph{poũchhāno}) is filed in CDIAL 8716 under Sanskrit \emph{prabhūta}, 'much, great', which lists Bengali \emph{paũchā}, 'to arrive'; how the sense moved is not set out there. Past: \bn{পৌঁছাল}, arrived.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{poũchhāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{poũchhāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmrā kôtô tāṛātāṛi poũchhābô, seṭā tomār opôr nirbhôr kôre.} — How fast we get there is up to you.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to burn down, then the Bengali for an explosion, then say \emph{poũchhāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা} (uddhār kôrā)}{উদ্ধার করা (uddhār kôrā)}]{\bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা} (uddhār kôrā) — to rescue}

\label{lesson:BN-C280-uddhar-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an explosion, then the Bengali for to arrive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা}} — \emph{uddhār kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rescue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দমকলের} \bn{লোকেরা} \bn{আগুন} \bn{থেকে} \bn{দুই} \bn{শিশুকে} \bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dômkôler lokerā āgun theke dui shishuke uddhār kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The firefighters rescued two children from the fire.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{শিশুটিকে} \bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini shishuṭike uddhār kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা}} (\emph{uddhār kôrā}) puts Sanskrit \emph{uddhāra}, 'raising, lifting up' (Monier-Williams), before \bn{করা}: to rescue is to lift someone out of danger.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uddhār kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dômkôler lokerā āgun theke dui shishuke uddhār kôrlô.} — The firefighters rescued two children from the fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an explosion, then the Bengali for to arrive, then say \emph{uddhār kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মই} (môi)}{মই (môi)}]{\bn{মই} (môi) — a ladder}

\label{lesson:BN-C280-moi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to arrive, then the Bengali for to rescue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মই}}
\textbf{\bn{মই}} — \emph{môi} — \textquotedblleft{}a ladder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তারা} \bn{জানালায়} \bn{একটা} \bn{মই} \bn{লাগাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tārā jānālāy ekṭā môi lāgālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They put a ladder up against the window.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মই}} (\emph{môi}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{matya}, a kind of harrow (CDIAL 9755); CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{moi} as both a harrow and a ladder.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সাইরেন} (sāiren)}{সাইরেন (sāiren)}]{\bn{সাইরেন} (sāiren) — a siren}

\label{lesson:BN-C280-sairen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to rescue, then the Bengali for a ladder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সাইরেন}}
\textbf{\bn{সাইরেন}} — \emph{sāiren} — \textquotedblleft{}a siren\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সাইরেন} \bn{শুনে} \bn{সবাই} \bn{রাস্তার} \bn{পাশে} \bn{দাঁড়াল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāiren shune sôbāi rāstār pāshe dā̃ṛālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When they heard the siren, everyone stood at the side of the road.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সাইরেন}} (\emph{sāiren}) is borrowed from English \emph{siren}, the warning wail of a fire engine or an ambulance; English took the name from the Sirens of Greek legend.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আশ্রয়} (āshrôy)}{আশ্রয় (āshrôy)}]{\bn{আশ্রয়} (āshrôy) — shelter; refuge}

\label{lesson:BN-C280-ashroy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a ladder, then the Bengali for a siren.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আশ্রয়}}
\textbf{\bn{আশ্রয়}} — \emph{āshrôy} — \textquotedblleft{}shelter; refuge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আগুনের} \bn{পরে} \bn{অনেক} \bn{পরিবার} \bn{স্কুলে} \bn{আশ্রয়} \bn{নিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āguner pôre ônek pôribār skule āshrôy nilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the fire, many families took shelter in the school.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আশ্রয়}} (\emph{āshrôy}) is Sanskrit \emph{āśraya}, that on which something leans or rests (Monier-Williams). \bn{আশ্রয়} \bn{নেওয়া}, to take shelter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a ladder, then the Bengali for a siren, then say \emph{āshrôy} again
\end{itemize}
